verdict.reasoning: Patient reports wheeze started about two days ago after cleaning with dust exposure: "it started, like, about two days ago" and "I was, like, cleaning the house. And, like, um, all this dust came out of the, the carpet."
Onset timing is described as about an hour after exposure: Doctor asks if it started then, and patient says it started "after maybe, uh, an hour or so."
Worse at night and progressive: Patient says, "Yeah. So, it get's a bit worse, um, at night, I find" and earlier confirms it has been getting worse over the past two days.

Shortness of breath and difficulty completing sentences: Patient says "I'm feeling like a little bit, uh, uh, short of breath" and "when I'm... talking... I start finding that, uh, sometimes, um, I'm unable to , complete my sentences."
No pleuritic pain and no dizziness/vertigo: To deep breath pain question patient replies, "Mmm, no, no. No pain" and to dizziness, "Uh, no. No dizziness. Uh, none of that."
Fluid intake: When asked about eating and drinking, patient says, "I think I'm having, like, you know, four or five glasses a day."

Childhood asthma with intermittent exercise-induced symptoms: Patient states, "I used to have, like, a bit of, um, asthma, uh, as a child" and later, "sometimes when I, um, run for, like, long periods, it can, it can start up a bit."
Seasonal hay fever: Patient says, "also in the summer I sometimes get, um, hay fever."

Has an inhaler from a couple months ago and has not taken anything for this episode: Patient confirms having "like, an asthma inhaler" and later, "I think I might have one from, like, a couple of months ago," and earlier answered "No" when asked, "have you taken anything for the wheeze?"
No regular antihistamines: When asked if she takes medications for hay fever, patient replies, "Not really," and later, "I don't have any antihistamines at home, unfortunately."
Prior steroid courses for asthma: Patient says, "I have, before, taken steroids for asthma."
Possible dust sensitivity: Patient says, "I've always thought that maybe I've got, uh, an allergy to, like, dust. Um, I think so."
No other known allergies: When asked "apart from this, do you know if you're allergic to anything?" patient replies, "not that I know of."

Description of acute wheeze/SOB after dust exposure is accurate; doctor explicitly frames differential as asthma vs allergy: "given you've got a history of asthma and hay fever. This could be one of two things. But, we want to rule out asthma or an allergy first."

History elements are supported and management is infrequent: Childhood asthma with exertional symptoms described, and doctor notes, "But, you don't see your doctor regularly for asthma?" with patient responding, "no, I don't," indicating suboptimal ongoing management.
Seasonal allergic rhinitis is equivalent to seasonal hay fever, which patient reports: "also in the summer I sometimes get, um, hay fever."

In-person GP/clinic visit and SpO2 check for asthma vs allergy: Doctor says, "what you'll need is visit one of our clinics, so we can do some more tests... use a small device on your finger, to check the amount of oxygen in your blood. And, from that we can tell if it's asthma or something else."
Letter to GP via app: Doctor states, "I'm gonna write a letter for your GP" and later, "you should get the letter over the app."

Advice to take OTC antihistamine now or buy en route: Doctor advises, "if you've got something, like an antihistamine... I would take one," and when patient says she has none, doctor adds, "You might be able to get one on your way to the doctor's surgery."
GP can prescribe antihistamine: Doctor says about antihistamine, "If not, they can prescribe you one."
Possible need for oral steroids: Doctor responds to prior steroid use, "you may need to take some steroids now. But, we... won't be able to know until we've done those tests first."
